answer: Stake-weighted reputation makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks collateral behind one identity vertex in the trust graph, and every deal adds weight along its edges. A sybil swarm can spin up thousands of sock puppets, but without locked stake and real counterparties they stay isolated, like voices echoing across a canyon with no bridge to the honest economy. Violet flags mark sudden clusters of new accounts trading only with each other, so an attacker must fund each fake identity and build genuine history — one fake vote costs more than it pays.
